description: Each media type's rate is the mean of its tracks' own Bytes/Milliseconds ratios.

b.request: Among media types that have at least one track with a matching media type, compute each media type's rate as the mean of its tracks' individual Bytes/Milliseconds ratios (tracks with NULL Bytes excluded from that mean), count the tracks per media type, then keep only media types whose rate exceeds the unweighted average of all media types' rates, and report each one's name, rate, track count, and difference from that average, unrounded
b.sql: WITH media_stats AS (SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name AS name, AVG(t.Bytes * 1.0 / NULLIF(t.Milliseconds, 0)) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM MediaType m JOIN Track t ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name), avg_rate AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate FROM media_stats) SELECT ms.name, ms.rate, ms.track_count, ms.rate - a.avg_rate AS difference FROM media_stats ms CROSS JOIN avg_rate a WHERE ms.rate > a.avg_rate;

a.request: Match each track to its media type, dropping tracks without a match. For each media type name, work out a rate by first dividing each track's `Bytes` by that same track's `Milliseconds` and then taking the plain average of those per-track ratios (skipping tracks where the ratio is missing), and count its tracks. Show only the media types whose rate is above the simple mean of all media types' rates (each type counted once). For those, show the name, the rate, the track count, and the rate minus that mean, all unrounded.
a.sql:
WITH type_rates AS (
  SELECT m.MediaTypeId,
         m.Name AS Name,
         AVG(CASE WHEN t.Milliseconds <> 0 THEN t.Bytes * 1.0 / t.Milliseconds END) AS Rate,
         COUNT(t.TrackId) AS TrackCount
  FROM Track t
  JOIN MediaType m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId
  GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name
),
stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(Rate) AS MeanRate FROM type_rates
)
SELECT tr.Name,
       tr.Rate,
       tr.TrackCount,
       tr.Rate - s.MeanRate AS RateMinusMean
FROM type_rates tr
CROSS JOIN stats s
WHERE tr.Rate > s.MeanRate;

c.request: Looking only at tracks that have a matching media type, what is each media type's bytes-per-millisecond rate (`Bytes` vs `Milliseconds`), and how many tracks does it have? Show only the media types whose rate is above the simple average of all media types' rates (each type counted once). For those, give the name, the rate, the track count, and how far the rate is above that average. Don't round anything. Each media type's rate is the mean of its tracks' own Bytes/Milliseconds ratios.
c.sql:
WITH media_rates AS (
  SELECT mt.MediaTypeId,
         mt.Name AS MediaTypeName,
         AVG(CAST(t.Bytes AS REAL) / t.Milliseconds) AS rate,
         COUNT(t.TrackId) AS track_count
  FROM Track t
  JOIN MediaType mt ON mt.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId
  WHERE t.Milliseconds > 0
  GROUP BY mt.MediaTypeId, mt.Name
),
avg_rate AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate FROM media_rates
)
SELECT mr.MediaTypeName AS name,
       mr.rate AS rate,
       mr.track_count AS track_count,
       mr.rate - ar.avg_rate AS diff_above_avg
FROM media_rates mr
CROSS JOIN avg_rate ar
WHERE mr.rate > ar.avg_rate;

d.request: For tracks with a matching media type, what is each media type's rate, defined as the mean of its tracks' individual Bytes/Milliseconds ratios? Include the number of tracks per media type. Show only the media types whose rate is above the simple average of all media types' rates (each media type counted once), and for each, give the name, the rate, the track count, and how far the rate exceeds that average. Do not round any values.
d.sql: WITH media_rates AS (SELECT mt.MediaTypeId, mt.Name, AVG(t.Bytes * 1.0 / t.Milliseconds) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM MediaType mt JOIN Track t ON t.MediaTypeId = mt.MediaTypeId GROUP BY mt.MediaTypeId, mt.Name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate FROM media_rates) SELECT mr.Name, mr.rate, mr.track_count, mr.rate - o.avg_rate AS excess_over_avg FROM media_rates mr CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE mr.rate > o.avg_rate;
